newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says no decision on tie-up with foreign bank.
newsitem.headline: NCB says no decision on tie-up with foreign bank.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Monday it had not decided anything about a possible equity tie-up with a foreign bank, as reported by a Japanese daily at the weekend.
"We have decided nothing," an NCB spokesman said without elaborating.
The Yomiuri Shimbun said on Saturday that the financially troubled bank was considering an equity tie-up with a foreign bank in its efforts to restructure its business.

The paper said the tie-up would initially be limited to a business alliance. It said the Ministry of Finance was considering the possibility of letting NCB become the first Japanese bank in which there was investment by a foreign bank, as part of Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulation.

Last week, NCB said it expected to unveil a restructuring plan in early April. The bank did not provide details of the plan but banking sources said it would include sales of real estate and shutting down some operations overseas.

The Finance Ministry, which has expressed all-out support for NCB, thinks it necessary for a foreign bank to take over NCB's business abroad in order to minimise the impact on its domestic business of withdrawing from overseas operations, the Yomiuri said.
